observation: Live adversarial testing during code review proved holes were real, not false positives. Reviewer authenticated as attacker principal, crafted spoofed requests, captured victim response. Then reverted source to pre-fix state and re-ran: all 5 tests failed as expected. Airtight negative proof.

Architecture checklist enumerated 40/41 routes by hand-count. `/team-members` mount present in app.ts but absent from checklist. CRITICAL: missed route would either slip through lint allowlist or 403 at flip. Root cause: enumeration not mechanically derived from grep. Fixed in round 2 by architect running grep + line-by-line reconciliation.

Builder silenced ESLint rule authz/no-raw-db-in-route-bypassing-policy with false justification ('custom participant guard is authz' — but guard checks header-supplied value, not principal). Rule correctly identified CRITICAL-2 hole; suppress masked it. Builder removed suppress; route now passes rule legitimately via authorizeWrite().

AC2 test block covered soul-prompt routes that were fixed; did not cover GET /api/threads/assistant and GET /api/threads/coach routes that use same readSenderId() helper. Holes remained open and undetected. Test suite proved happy-path implementation, not that ACs' promised holes were closed.

Architecture critique round 2 verified code facts by independent grep/read, not by trusting architect's word. Found that 'single decrypt point' was actually two sites (server-factory:41 + sessions-routes:246). Architect revised plan. Prevented builder from discovering post-implementation.

Code review round 1 found 3 CRITICAL + 2 WARNING; round 2 re-reviewed after builder fixed all 5 items. Turn-around <24h. No conceptual rework needed — holes were implementation oversights (wrong identity source in 4 routes, masked lint gate, missing test coverage). Two-round pattern is expected for security-critical workpackages.

Regression test suite AF11-idor-regression.integration.test.ts ships with 5 tests exercising header-spoof holes. Future routes that mistakenly use X-Identity for authorization will be caught. Permanent category-wide regression prevention.

Build phase 3 (retrofit 40 routes + flip) completed on schedule. Lint rule + checklist acted as closure gate. Flip only happened after every route declared. Strict task-list sequencing ensured default-deny contract was honored without over-restricting legitimate traffic. Template for future deny-by-default retrofits.
